study: studies/end-to-end/xes3g5m-kc-tree-control (kc_tree.py) -- XES3G5M expert KC-route tree vs same-shape deranged and reversed trees
note: THE EXPERT TREE'S EDGES ARE A CONTROLLED NULL. Pre-registered at dfc8545 before learner data was read; e2e.py's split, difficulty offset, IRLS model, AUC and paired learner bootstrap (B = 200) imported, and its published M1/M2 AUCs reproduced exactly. Floors pass (tree: planted 5/5, null 0/10; family: 5/5, 0/10). V1 TREE EQUIVALENT TO ITS DERANGEMENT: real KC-parent links minus five depth-matched derangements of the same forest (559 links, no real link kept) +0.000037 [+0.000010, +0.000063] AUC, 3,630 TEST learners; V2 TREE ADDS NOTHING over expert KCs (+0.000051); direction CLAIMED by +0.00002, interval includes 0, not verdict-bearing. Secondary V3 FAMILY EQUIVALENT TO ITS DERANGEMENT by the +/-0.001 rule, but signed and above zero: route-family pooling +0.000724 [+0.000638, +0.000816], +0.001245 [+0.001118, +0.001372] at cold start (descriptive); deranged families reach 0.52-0.61 of the real family's history coverage, so curriculum co-location is a rival reading. Turns the XES3G5M authors' unexplained KC-route null (lit. review 5.9) into a controlled null in e2e.py's model and extends F5: expert edges add no more than LLM-built ones; grouping, not direction, carries the small gain. The authors' early-fusion deep models were not run (no torch, CPU only). Moves nothing.
